To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The collective parameter δ = (β R) 2 / 2J + 1, where βR is the deformation length, is predicted to be a function of the probe in inelastic scattering, and the variation of δ with probe is experimentally verified in the case of 0 + →2 + transitions in nuclei.

the variation of βR for a fixed probe and nucleus is in agreement with a first-order reaction mechanism and that the variation of δ with probe and nucleus is consistent with a core polarization model.

(1) the collective parameter δ, obtained from distorted wave Born approximation analyses of inelastic hadron (π, K, N, and Λ) scattering data, is systematically larger for neutron transitions than for proton transitions; (2) this systematic difference is consistent with a core polarization model of the transition; and (3) the observed variation of δ with probe, which is predicted by the core polarization model, is consistent with the validity of the reaction mechanism used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of first-order reaction mechanisms to the description of the elastic and inelastic scattering of hadrons.
the study of collective excitations in nuclei.
the study of the structure of nuclei through inelastic hadron (pion, proton, neutron) scattering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the first-order reaction theory provides an adequate description of the data and that the observed variation of βR is a result of core polarization.
first-order reaction theory, with its inherent approximations and assumptions, is adequate for the description of the data.
first-order DWIA calculations of inelastic scattering are adequate for the analysis of the data, and that the observed variation of βR is consistent with the predictions of core polarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the first-order reaction mechanisms is adequate to describe both the electromagnetic and inelastic hadron reactions for 0 + to 2 + transitions.
first-order calculations, with a core-polarization mechanism, are adequate for the description of the collective parameters for inelastic scattering of hadrons from closed shell nuclei.

the distorted wave approximation is adequate for the description of inelastic hadron reactions at energies below ≈ 200 MeV, that the collective parameter δ is an observable which can be determined with a high accuracy and that the observed variation of δ with probe is consistent with a core polarization model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probe dependence of βR provides a sensitive probe of nuclear structure, which is not available from electromagnetic probes.
first order DWBA calculations can accurately describe inelastic hadron reactions.
the collective parameter β R can be determined to a high precision from inelastic hadron data and that the first-order reaction model is a good approximation.
